parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of same-sex conduct or gender expression and no documented border, facility or care ban reduce visitor exposure, but documented police targeting of transgender women, street harassment and abuse, arrests perceived as because trans, and no operative anti-discrimination recourse leave an outed visitor vulnerable. City-level police abuse is the worst documented feature, with no imprisonment or lethal pathway documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No border refusal, marker mismatch or X-marker practice documented; visitor uses home passport.
entry_documents.protection: No criminalisation of gender expression documented; official tourism welcome posture noted.
entry_documents.interaction: Absence of domestic legal gender recognition is resident-facing and, without documented border application, is not treated as visitor exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 2016 survey reported about 38% of surveyed transgender women arrested, over 90% saying because transgender; sampling frame not stated. One city's police targeted transgender sex workers, forced bathing in dirty river water, sometimes naked, and expulsion.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No published custody-placement regulation documented. February 2025 praise statement described transfer after sex-change surgery from men's to women's facility only.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest or detention could expose a non-surgery visitor to men's-facility placement; no documented policy for that group. Sex-work context limits direct transfer to non-sex-work visitors, but shows police practice.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No bathroom, locker-room, ward or other facility-access restriction documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No operative national or city facility rule documented to examine; city variation is documented mainly for policing and scene, not facility law.

care_services.exposure: No documented refusal, medication confiscation or visitor care denial. Gender-affirming surgery not legally available is resident-facing.
care_services.protection: 2017 foreign-government report found no official discrimination in health care based on sexual orientation; trans-specific visitor care protection not documented.
care_services.interaction: Resident surgery restriction does not establish denial of visitor routine or emergency care.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No trans-specific offence documented, but police practice targeting transgender sex workers and reported arrests because transgender indicate threat-framing in street enforcement in at least one city.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Never criminalised same-sex activity; UPR recommendations accepted 2019 and 2024, Pride and visible scene in two cities, tourism welcome campaign endorsed.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Accepted recommendations and disputed 2015 protection claim have no enacted statutory protection documented, so they do not offset documented police practice.

minors_guardians.exposure: No traveller-facing minor, guardian, school-placement or family-travel restriction documented. Family rejection and forced rehabilitation documented are resident/family-sphere matters.
minors_guardians.interaction: Documented family rejection does not establish risk to a visiting minor travelling with a guardian; no applicable rule documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: More than 135 harassment/abuse cases against transgender women recorded by national human-rights organisation; more than 100 violence/abuse incidents reported in 2017. Counts are monitoring figures, not prevalence rates. Police in one city were documented perpetrators against transgender sex workers.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No operative anti-discrimination or hate-crime recourse documented; information-ministry request to media to stop mocking LGBT people and tourism welcome are not enforceable remedies.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Street harassment plus police perpetration in one city, without documented prosecution of attackers, increases risk if outed, especially in that city; scene and Pride in two cities indicate some public presence but not protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination statute documented; cabinet spokesman claim of existing protection disputed; no remedy for police abuse documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: UN expert visit and UPR acceptances are process signals, not operative visitor remedies.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty remains on custody placement for non-surgery prisoners, other cities' policing, and arrest survey representativeness; these unknowns are not treated as safety.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in documented police stops, humiliation and weak complaints handling, but case lacks routine passport confiscation, fines and compulsory interviews for all visitors, and police abuse is documented principally against transgender sex workers in one city, so slightly higher than 0.35.

Higher than this case: there harassment is sporadic and charges uncommon, whereas here police targeting, forced naked bathing and expulsion, and reported arrests because transgender are documented, with no operative legal remedy, so materially lower than 0.55.

Higher than this case: 0.25-C has birth-sex prison housing with frequent assaults and criminalised cross-dressing enabling arrests; here no such custody rule is documented beyond a surgery-gated transfer statement, and no cross-dressing offence, so lower risk than 0.25.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is permissive on paper—no same-sex or expression criminalisation, Pride, visible scene and official welcome—but street-level enforcement is the operative risk. Police targeting in one city, widespread recorded harassment, and reported trans-based arrests combine with no enacted anti-discrimination protection or documented remedy for attackers. No border, facility, care or minor-specific visitor restriction is documented, and imprisonment or execution for being trans is not documented, keeping the case in the elevated-risk range rather than high/severe.
